title: Sergey Brin
wiki_lead:
Sergey Mikhailovich Brin (Russian: Сергей Михайлович Брин; born August 21, 1973) is an American computer scientist and businessman who co-founded Google with Larry Page. He was the president of Google's parent company, Alphabet Inc., until stepping down from the role in 2019. He and Page remain at Alphabet as co-founders, controlling shareholders, and board members. Brin is a centibillionaire and among the richest people in the world; as of 18 October 2026, his estimated net worth is US$257.1 billion.
Born into a Russian-Jewish family in Moscow, Soviet Union, Brin immigrated to the United States at the age of six. He earned his bachelor's degree at the University of Maryland, College Park, following in his father's and grandfather's footsteps by studying mathematics as well as computer science. After graduation, in 1993, he enrolled in Stanford University to pursue a PhD in computer science. There, Brin met Page, with whom he built a web search engine. The program became popular at Stanford, and he discontinued his PhD studies to start Google in Susan Wojcicki's garage in Menlo Park, California. In 2023, Brin came out of retirement to contribute to AI research at Alphabet.

Early life and education
Brin was born into a Russian-Jewish family on August 21, 1973, in Moscow, then the capital of the Soviet Union. Both of his parents, Mikhail and Eugenia "Genia" Brin, graduated from Moscow State University (MSU). The former is a retired mathematics professor at the University of Maryland (UMD), and the latter was a researcher at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center.
The family lived in a three-room apartment in central Moscow, which they also shared with Brin's paternal grandmother. In 1977, after returning from a mathematics conference in Warsaw, his father announced that, because of antisemitism in the Soviet Union, it was time for them to emigrate. The family formally applied for their exit visa in September 1978, and as a result, Brin's father was "promptly fired". Brin's mother had to leave her job for related reasons. For the next eight months, without any steady income, the couple were forced to take on temporary jobs as they waited, afraid that their request would be denied as it was for many refuseniks. In May 1979, the Brin family were granted their official exit visas and were allowed to leave the country.
The family lived in Vienna and Paris while Brin's father secured a teaching position at UMD with help from Anatole Katok. During this time, they received support and assistance from the Hebrew Immigrant Aid Society. The Brin family arrived in the United States in October 1979. They lived in the Long Island, New York, house of a friend from Moscow before moving to Maryland, where they rented a house in a lower-middle-class neighborhood near UMD's campus.

grok_lead: Sergey Mikhailovich Brin (born August 21, 1973) is a Russian-born American computer scientist and entrepreneur who co-founded Google with Larry Page in 1998 while pursuing graduate studies at Stanford University. Born in Moscow to Jewish mathematician parents facing antisemitism in the Soviet Union, Brin immigrated to the United States with his family at age six in 1979, settling in Maryland where his father joined the University of Maryland faculty. He earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and computer science from the University of Maryland before enrolling at Stanford for a Ph.D. in computer science, where he met Page and collaborated on analyzing the web's link structure. Together, Brin and Page developed the PageRank algorithm, which evaluates webpage importance based on incoming links to deliver more relevant search results, forming the core of Google 's search engine and enabling its rapid growth into a dominant internet service. The company went public in 2004, creating immense wealth for its founders; Brin served as Google's president of technology and later as president of Alphabet Inc., the 2015 parent holding company, until stepping down from executive roles in 2019 while retaining board membership and significant share control. In recent years, Brin has re-engaged actively with Google, focusing on artificial intelligence development, including contributions to models like Gemini, amid competitive pressures in the sector. As of 2026 he remains hands-on in Gemini development and Alphabet's broader AI strategy, having described his 2019 retirement as a "big mistake" after Google's earlier underinvestment in the field. His work extends to philanthropy through the Brin Wojcicki Foundation and investments in longevity research via ventures like Calico, reflecting interests in health and technology beyond search.
